newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HOLLIOAKE, 19, INCLUDED IN ENGLAND TEST SQUAD.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HOLLIOAKE, 19, INCLUDED IN ENGLAND TEST SQUAD.

text.p: Ben Hollioake is expected to become England's youngest test player for almost 50 years at Trent Bridge on Thursday.
The 19-year-old Surrey all-rounder was included on Sunday in a 13-man squad for the fifth test against Australia.
His brother Adam, seven years his senior, is also in the squad.
Chairman of selectors David Graveney said the choice of the Hollioake brothers and the recall of Devon Malcolm, England's only genuine fast bowler, represented "an injection of new spirit".
The Hollioakes' test call-up followed heavy defeats in the third and fourth matches which left England 2-1 down in the Ashes series.
Both played significant roles in England's 3-0 win over the touring team in the one-day series preceding the tests.
Assuming Ben plays, he will become England's youngest test player since 18-year-old Brian Close made his debut in 1949.
"Thank goodness Adam is in the squad as well," said a delighted Ben. "If he hadn't made it, I wouldn't have been able to go home." The two brothers share a flat.
With opener Mark Butcher dropped along with all-rounder Mark Ealham and fast-medium bowler Mike Smith, wicketkeeper Alec Stewart is almost certain to open the innings with skipper Mike Atherton.
John Crawley will fill Stewart's normal role at number three. The Hollioakes are likely to bat at six and seven.
A decision on the bowling line-up will not be taken until after an inspection of the Nottingham pitch.
